'''Robert Anthony Martienssen''' (born December 21, 1960)<ref name="WhosWho"/> is a British plant biologist, [[Howard Hughes Medical Institute]]–[[Gordon and Betty Moore Foundation]] investigator,<ref>{{cite web|title = Robert A. Martienssen, PhD {{!}} HHMI.org|url = http://www.hhmi.org/scientists/robert-martienssen|accessdate = 2015-09-27}}</ref> and professor at [[Cold Spring Harbor Laboratory]], US.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.cshl.edu/Faculty/Rob-Martienssen.html |title=CSHLRob Martienssen |website=www.cshl.edu |access-date=17 January 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150103074206/http://www.cshl.edu/Faculty/Rob-Martienssen.html |archive-date=3 January 2015 |url-status=dead}}</ref><ref name=PichuginaSugawara2016>{{cite journal|last1=Pichugina|first1=T.|last2=Sugawara|first2=T.|last3=Kaykov|first3=A.|last4=Schierding|first4=W.|last5=Masuda|first5=K.|last6=Uewaki|first6=J.|last7=Grand|first7=R. M.|title=A diffusion model for the coordination of DNA replication in Schizosaccharomyces pombe|journal=[[Scientific Reports]]|volume=6|year=2016|article-number=18757|doi=10.1038/srep18757|doi-access=free|pmid=26729303|pmc=4700429|bibcode=2016NatSR...618757P}} {{open access}}</ref><ref name="QuadranaBortolini Silveira2016">{{cite journal|last1=Quadrana|first1=Leandro|last2=Bortolini Silveira|first2=Amanda|last3=Mayhew|first3=George F|last4=LeBlanc|first4=Chantal|last5=Martienssen|first5=Robert A|last6=Jeddeloh|first6=Jeffrey A|last7=Colot|first7=Vincent|title=The Arabidopsis thaliana mobilome and its impact at the species level|journal=[[eLife]]|volume=5|year=2016|article-number=e15716 |doi=10.7554/eLife.15716|pmid=27258693|pmc=4917339 |doi-access=free }} {{open access}}</ref><ref name=scopus>{{Scopus|id=7007149382}}</ref>

== Education ==
Robert Martienssen attended [[Emmanuel College, Cambridge]],<ref name="WhosWho"/> completing his BA in 1982 and continuing on to his [[PhD]] in 1986 on the [[molecular genetics]] of [[alpha-amylase]] [[gene family|gene families]] in [[common wheat]],<ref name=phd>{{cite thesis|degree=PhD|publisher=University of Cambridge|title=The molecular genetics of alpha-amylase gene families in wheat (Triticum aestivum L.).|first= Robert Anthony|last=Martienssen|date=1986|url=http://idiscover.lib.cam.ac.uk/primo-explore/fulldisplay?docid=44CAM_ALMA21429714900003606&context=L&vid=44CAM_PROD&search_scope=SCOP_CAM_ALL&tab=cam_lib_coll&lang=en_US|id={{EThOS|uk.bl.ethos.382600}}|website=lib.cam.ac.uk|oclc=59751016}}</ref> supervised by [[David Baulcombe]].<ref name="PlantaeInterview">{{Cite web|url=https://plantae.org/luminaries-rob-martienssen/|title = Luminaries: Rob Martienssen|date = 13 February 2017}}</ref> He received an EMBO postdoctoral fellowship to travel to the [[University of California, Berkeley]] where he was a postdoctoral researcher with [[Michael Freeling]] from 1986 to 1988 where he showed that changes methylation of transposons could be associated with genetically heritable changes in the phenotype of corn plants.<ref>{{cite journal|doi=10.1101/gad.4.3.331|title=Somatically heritable switches in the DNA modification of Mu transposable elements monitored with a suppressible mutant in maize|year=1990|last1=Martienssen|first1=R.|last2=Barkan|first2=A.|last3=Taylor|first3=W. C.|last4=Freeling|first4=M.|journal=Genes & Development|volume=4|issue=3|pages=331–343|pmid=2159936|doi-access=free}}</ref> In 1989 he was hired as a principal investigator at [[Cold Spring Harbor Laboratory]].<ref name="PlantaeInterview" />

==Research and career==
Martienssen has made major discoveries relating to the way plants control the expression of their genes. K.|title=The B73 Maize Genome: Complexity, Diversity, and Dynamics|journal=Science|volume=326|issue=5956|year=2009|pages=1112–1115|doi=10.1126/science.1178534|pmid=19965430|bibcode=2009Sci...326.1112S|display-authors=29|url=https://lib.dr.iastate.edu/cgi/viewcontent.cgi?article=1206&context=stat_las_pubs}}</ref> [[yeast]]<ref name=PichuginaSugawara2016/> and the weed ''[[Arabidopsis]]'', he focuses on the chemical modifications to [[DNA]] that determine which genes are active — a process known as [[epigenetics]].<ref name=frs/><ref name=SlotkinMartienssen2007/>

Martienssen's work explains the effect on plants of ‘jumping genes’, or DNA [[transposable element]]s, reported in 1951 by [[Barbara McClintock]], whom he worked alongside early in his career. He discovered that small pieces of [[RNA]], in association with proteins of the [[Argonaute]] family, silence transposons in seeds so that [[gene expression]] remains stable from one generation to the next.<ref name=frs/>

His work was cited by the journal ''[[Science (journal)|Science]]'' as part of its ''Breakthrough of the Year: 2002'' feature<ref name=breakthrough>{{cite web|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20160322053532/http://www.sciencemag.org/news/2002/12/breakthrough-year-small-rnas|archivedate=2016-03-22|url=https://www.science.org/content/article/breakthrough-year-small-rnas|year=2002|website=sciencemag.org|title=Breakthrough of the Year: Small RNAs|first=Jennifer|last=Couzin-Frankel}}</ref> on [[small RNA]]s. He has extended his epigenetic studies from seeds to [[pollen]], and his discoveries have implications for [[plant breeding]] — including hybrid cloning — and the development of [[biofuel]]s.<ref name=frs/>
